attackLog.incidentOrCve: Cursor Marketplace Supply Chain Breach (Claude Code)

attackLog.immediateSolution: Immediately revoke and roll compromised vendor API tokens, enforce extension code signing validation, and restrict developer IDE plugin installations via MDM policy.

deepDives.title: Cursor & Fireworks AI Secret Compromise: Weaponization of Developer AI Extensions
deepDives.whatHappened: Adversaries exfiltrated an internal API key issued to AI infrastructure vendor Fireworks AI. Leveraging this credential, attackers gained read and publishing access to upload a trojanized version of the official Claude Code extension onto the Cursor developer marketplace, threatening hundreds of enterprise development teams with source code interception and terminal credential scraping.
deepDives.technicalMechanism: The stolen API token lacked role-based scoping and administrative network context validation. Upon accessing the internal marketplace registry, attackers modified the extension manifest to include a secondary JavaScript payload disguised as telemetry initialization. Once developer IDEs automatically updated the extension, the payload spawned an out-of-band child process to harvest developer environment variables (.env files, AWS/GitHub CLI tokens) and exfiltrated them via encrypted HTTPS POST requests to attacker-controlled C2 infrastructure.
deepDives.asciiFlow: [Compromised Fireworks AI Key] ──► [Cursor Registry Push API] ──► [Trojanized Claude Extension] ──► [Developer IDE Auto-Update] ──► [Exfiltrated .env & API Keys]
remediation: Revoke and rotate all developer environment tokens, cloud access keys, and SSH identities across all workstations running the Claude Code extension.
Implement mandatory cryptographic package signing and dual-authorization verification gates prior to publishing any IDE marketplace plugin update.
Deploy EDR threat hunting queries across engineering fleet to detect anomalous IDE child process executions (e.g., node/cursor spawning curl, bash, or certutil).
deepDives.lessonsLearned: Third-party AI service integrations represent an extension of the primary software supply chain. Machine-to-machine API tokens granted to partners must be tightly scoped with least privilege, bound to egress IP ranges, and never grant implicit publisher rights to critical software distribution pipelines.

deepDives.title: Check Point PHP2Shell Exploitation Pivoting to VMware ESXi Hypervisor Wiper Execution
deepDives.whatHappened: Threat actors are weaponizing command injection vulnerabilities within perimeter Check Point Security Gateways (known colloquially as PHP2Shell chains) to achieve initial network foothold. Rather than maintaining quiet persistence, attackers rapidly pivoted across management interfaces to deliver destructive wiper payloads directly onto VMware ESXi hypervisors, destroying enterprise storage partitions and backup volumes.
deepDives.technicalMechanism: Attackers issue crafted HTTP requests to the Check Point web-based gateway management interface, bypassing authentication filters to execute arbitrary shell commands under web server privileges. Gaining control of the perimeter device, the threat actor exploits pre-existing administrative trust relationships, extracting saved administrative credentials and pivoting into the internal hypervisor management network. Using automated shell scripts, the adversary establishes SSH sessions to VMware ESXi nodes, stops all guest virtual machines, and invokes raw disk-level commands (e.g., 'dd if=/dev/urandom of=/dev/disks/...') to irreversibly destroy VMDK volumes and datastores.
deepDives.asciiFlow: [Attacker HTTP Payload] ──► [Check Point PHP2Shell RCE] ──► [Extracted Admin Credentials] ──► [ESXi Management SSH Pivot] ──► [Raw Disk Wiper Execution]
remediation: Apply emergency firmware security updates to all internet-facing Check Point Gateway appliances and revoke administrative sessions.
Sever all direct routable access between edge gateway interfaces and core hypervisor management subnets (ESXi/vCenter), placing management interfaces behind strict multi-factor jump hosts.
Audit ESXi host logs for unauthorized SSH service activations and anomalous shell commands manipulating virtual storage controllers.
deepDives.lessonsLearned: Perimeter firewalls and security appliances must be treated as untrusted zero-trust edges rather than trusted internal network pivots. Hardware gateways should never maintain direct, uninspected administrative pathways into foundational virtualization and recovery infrastructure.

deepDives.title: Trezor Safe 5 Supply Chain Interception: Cellular Hardware Implant Implantation
deepDives.whatHappened: Hardware cryptocurrency wallet vendor Trezor confirmed that three Safe 5 devices distributed through Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis were modified in transit with malicious hardware implants. The covert micro-circuitry successfully intercepted 12- and 24-word BIP39 seed phrases during initial wallet generation and transmitted them directly to an adversary over cellular frequencies, bypassing endpoint isolation completely.
deepDives.technicalMechanism: The physical attackers carefully de-soldered the OEM casing to avoid tripping tamper-evident enclosure seals. They installed an ultra-miniature hardware daughterboard tapped directly into the physical display and touchscreen serial bus traces (I2C/SPI). When the user generates a recovery phrase on-screen, the hardware implant captures the raw display framebuffers or bus signals, decodes the mnemonic words, and queues them into an integrated micro-GSM modem that broadcasts the exfiltrated seed phrase over 2G/LTE frequency bands to attacker infrastructure.
deepDives.asciiFlow: [Factory Shipment] ──► [Interception & Implant Soldered] ──► [User Enters Seed Phrase] ──► [Implant Intercepts I2C/SPI] ──► [Cellular Radio Exfiltration]
remediation: Procure hardware security devices and cryptographic key tokens exclusively through direct manufacturer channels with tamper-evident transport bags.
Conduct optical and ultrasonic non-destructive verification of high-risk cryptographic hardware before provisioning organizational keys.
Instruct personnel managing cold-storage infrastructure to verify hardware enclosure weight, seams, and perform initial device staging inside RF-shielded Faraday enclosures.
deepDives.lessonsLearned: Air-gapping endpoints is ineffective if the physical hardware bus is compromised prior to deployment. Critical cryptographic systems must adopt end-to-end cryptographic supply-chain attestations, physical tamper-resistant micro-coatings, and radio-frequency RF audits prior to production commissioning.

dailyQuestions.scenario: A development team utilizing an AI-assisted IDE reports that a popular third-party coding extension was recently compromised on the vendor's marketplace after an external service API key was leaked. An attacker uploaded a malicious update that attempts to steal local environment secrets. Which of the following technical controls represents the MOST effective immediate mitigation to prevent automated installation of untrusted or modified IDE extensions across the enterprise?
options: A) Deploy an intrusion detection system (IDS) at the perimeter to inspect encrypted HTTPS traffic.
B) Configure enterprise IDE policy to disable public marketplace installations and enforce an internally managed, code-signed private extension repository.
C) Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) on all developer laptop login accounts.
D) Increase endpoint logging frequency for developer workstations to a 30-day retention policy.
dailyQuestions.rationale: Enforcing an internally managed, code-signed private extension repository via enterprise MDM/IDE policy prevents developers from pulling compromised or unverified packages directly from public marketplaces. Option A is ineffective against pinned TLS traffic without complex interception, Option C addresses interactive user identity rather than extension execution, and Option D is a passive detective control rather than a preventive mitigation.

dailyQuestions.scenario: An enterprise architecture team is designing an integration architecture for autonomous LLM agents that process semi-structured vendor invoices received via email and initiate database updates for accounts payable accounts. In light of recent indirect prompt injection threats capable of manipulating transaction details, which of the following security architectures provides the HIGHEST level of resilience and non-repudiation?
options: A) Pass invoice email text through a fine-tuned LLM classifier to filter out known malicious system prompt keywords prior to agent consumption.
B) Isolate the AI agent in a containerized environment and allow it to issue direct parameterized SQL UPDATE commands using least privilege.

C) Decouple agent inference from execution by structuring the LLM output into an unexecuted draft state, requiring cryptographically signed out-of-band human-in-the-loop (HITL) approval before dispatching transactional API calls.
D) Implement TLS 1.3 encryption across all internal messaging queues connecting the invoice email ingestion daemon to the LLM agent cluster.
dailyQuestions.rationale: Indirect prompt injection cannot be deterministically resolved through token blacklisting or prompt classifiers (Option A), as natural language variations routinely bypass static or model-based filters. Allowing direct database execution (Option B) exposes the system to unauthorized modifications regardless of parameterized SQL. Option D only protects transit confidentiality. Decoupling inference from execution and mandating an out-of-band, cryptographically signed Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) workflow ensures that autonomous agent hallucinations or injected overrides cannot execute high-risk financial state changes unilaterally.

detectionRules.title: Anomalous IDE Process Spawning Interactive Shell or Network Tooling
detectionRules.code:
title: Suspicious Process Spawning from Developer IDE
id: d6e834b9-8c21-4fa1-b1e9-74d39bc52026
status: production
description: Detects code editor processes (Cursor, VS Code, JetBrains) directly spawning system shells or networking utilities associated with trojanized extensions.
author: CyberDefense SecOps
date: 2026/11/15
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\cursor.exe'
      - '\Code.exe'
      - '\idea64.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\bash.exe'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate developer terminal sessions initiated interactively by the user (correlate with parent process command-line arguments).
level: high
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.t1195.002
